baselinePractice.name: Platform Adoption Kernel
baselinePractice.description: The Platform Adoption Kernel establishes the universal foundation for platform transformations, organized into the three standard Essence Areas of Concern.

focuses.name: Value
focuses.description: Focuses on business justification, financial management, and organizational alignment.

focuses.name: Solution
focuses.description: Encapsulates the design, provisioning, optimization, and the hosted items running on the platform foundation.

focuses.name: Endeavor
focuses.description: Governs the execution of the transformation, encompassing people, processes, and policies.

alphas.name: Opportunity
alphas.description: The foundational business drivers dictating the platform transformation.

states.name: Initiated
states.description: The desire to adopt a platform is identified.

states.name: Determined
states.description: The value and parameters of the platform are quantified.

states.name: Value Established
states.description: The platform's value is accepted by sponsors.

states.name: Viable
states.description: The platform adoption is deemed feasible.

states.name: Addressed
states.description: The platform provides the intended operational capabilities.

states.name: Benefit Accrued
states.description: Return on investment is realized.

alphas.name: Stakeholders
alphas.description: The people, groups, or organizations who affect or are affected by the platform.

states.name: Recognized
states.description: All key stakeholder groups are identified.

states.name: Represented
states.description: Representatives for platform consumers and business units are appointed.

states.name: Involved
states.description: Representatives actively participate in platform design.

states.name: In Agreement
states.description: Stakeholders agree on platform capabilities and constraints.

states.name: Satisfied For Deployment
states.description: Stakeholders accept the initial platform foundation.

states.name: Satisfied In Use
states.description: Stakeholders successfully use the platform for operations.

alphas.name: Platform Value And Economics
alphas.description: The realization of financial and strategic return on investment.

states.name: Identified
states.description: TCO drafted, drivers documented.

states.name: Modeled
states.description: Financial model created, funding secured.

states.name: Allocated
states.description: Budgets assigned, tagging enforced.

states.name: Optimized
states.description: Resources actively rightsized.

states.name: Sustained
states.description: Cost optimization is a continuous automated process.

alphas.name: Requirements
alphas.description: What the platform must do to address the opportunity and satisfy the stakeholders.

states.name: Conceived
states.description: The need for a new platform has been agreed.

states.name: Bounded
states.description: The purpose and extent of the new platform are clear.

states.name: Coherent
states.description: The requirements provide a consistent description of the essential characteristics.

states.name: Acceptable
states.description: The requirements describe a platform that is acceptable to the stakeholders.

states.name: Addressed
states.description: Enough of the requirements have been addressed to satisfy the need.

states.name: Fulfilled
states.description: The requirements that have been addressed fully satisfy the need.

alphas.name: Platform
alphas.description: The foundational environment serving as the scalable backbone.

states.name: Envisioned
states.description: Target architecture style selected.

states.name: Baselined
states.description: Core platform foundation and shared environments defined.

states.name: Provisioned
states.description: IaC templates have deployed the baseline.

states.name: Hosting Assets
states.description: The platform is formally accepting Platform Asset deployments.

states.name: Evolving
states.description: Platform is being continuously adapted to address the evolving needs of its users.

alphas.name: Platform Consumption Interface
alphas.description: The unified boundary abstracting platform complexity for consumers.

states.name: Scoped
states.description: Consumer personas identified.

states.name: Unified
states.description: Cohesive consumption strategy established.

states.name: Self Service
states.description: Consumers can autonomously provision.

states.name: Governed
states.description: Interface automatically enforces rules.

states.name: Optimized
states.description: Interface adapts based on telemetry.

alphas.name: Platform Asset
alphas.description: The abstract items (e.g., containers, models, services) hosted by and dependent upon the platform.

states.name: Identified
states.description: Need for the asset on the platform is recognized.

states.name: Integrated
states.description: Configured to natively consume platform services.

states.name: Operational
states.description: Deployed and actively running on the platform infrastructure.

states.name: Value Yielding
states.description: Leverages platform scale to deliver business value.

states.name: Optimized
states.description: Resource consumption is highly efficient.

states.name: Retired
states.description: Safely decoupled and removed from the platform.

alphas.name: Work
alphas.description: Activity involving mental or physical effort done in order to achieve a result.

states.name: Initiated
states.description: The work has been requested.

states.name: Prepared
states.description: All pre-conditions for starting the work have been met.

states.name: Started
states.description: The work is proceeding.

states.name: Under Control
states.description: The work is going well, risks are under control.

states.name: Concluded
states.description: The work to produce the results has been concluded.

states.name: Closed
states.description: All remaining housekeeping tasks have been completed.

alphas.name: Team
alphas.description: A group of people actively engaged in the development, maintenance, delivery, or support of a specific platform.

states.name: Seeded
states.description: The team's mission is clear and the know-how needed is in place.

states.name: Formed
states.description: The team has been populated with enough committed people.

states.name: Collaborating
states.description: The team members are working together as one unit.

states.name: Performing
states.description: The team is working effectively and efficiently.

states.name: Adjourned
states.description: The team is no longer accountable for carrying out its mission.

alphas.name: Way Of Working
alphas.description: The tailored set of practices and tools used by a team to guide and support their work.

states.name: Principles Established
states.description: The principles and constraints are established.

states.name: Foundation Established
states.description: The key practices and tools are selected.

states.name: In Use
states.description: Some members of the team are using, and adapting, the way-of-working.

states.name: In Place
states.description: All team members are using the way of working to accomplish their work.

states.name: Working Well
states.description: The team's way of working is working well for the team.

states.name: Retired
states.description: The way of working is no longer in use by the team.

states.name: Scoped
states.description: Regulatory requirements identified.

states.name: Documented
states.description: Policies are written and approved.

states.name: Audited
states.description: Platform monitored for configuration drift.

states.name: Enforced
states.description: Automated guardrails physically prevent non-compliance.

states.name: Automated
states.description: Remediation occurs instantaneously.

activitySpaces.name: Explore Possibilities
activitySpaces.description: Explore the possibilities presented by the creation of a new or improved platform.

activitySpaces.name: Understand Stakeholder Needs
activitySpaces.description: Engage with the stakeholders to understand their needs and ensure that the right results are produced.

activitySpaces.name: Ensure Stakeholder Satisfaction
activitySpaces.description: Share the results of the development work with the stakeholders to gain their acceptance of the platform produced.

activitySpaces.name: Understand Platform Opportunity
activitySpaces.description: Defines the overarching platform strategy and aligns executive sponsorship.

activitySpaces.name: Optimize Platform Value
activitySpaces.description: The continuous process of forecasting costs and maximizing financial efficiency.

activitySpaces.name: Understand The Requirements
activitySpaces.description: Establish a shared understanding of what the platform to be produced must do.

activitySpaces.name: Automate Platform Provisioning
activitySpaces.description: The automation engineering of the platform for its target operating environment.

activitySpaces.name: Automate Platform Testing
activitySpaces.description: Verify that the platform produced meets the stakeholders' requirements through automated means.

activitySpaces.name: Deploy The Platform
activitySpaces.description: Take the tested platform and make it available for use.

activitySpaces.name: Operate The Platform
activitySpaces.description: Support the use of the platform in the live environment.

activitySpaces.name: Architect Platform Foundation
activitySpaces.description: Designing the core platform infrastructure topology and shared services.

activitySpaces.name: Engineer Platform Interfaces
activitySpaces.description: Building the APIs or Internal Developer Portals (IDPs) allowing self-service.

activitySpaces.name: Host And Operate Assets
activitySpaces.description: The continuous lifecycle management of items running on the platform.

activitySpaces.name: Prepare To Do The Work
activitySpaces.description: Set up the team and its working environment. Understand and commit to completing the work.

activitySpaces.name: Coordinate Activity
activitySpaces.description: Co-ordinate and direct the team's work. This includes all ongoing planning and re-planning.

activitySpaces.name: Support The Team
activitySpaces.description: Help the team members to help themselves, collaborate, and improve their way of working.

activitySpaces.name: Track Progress
activitySpaces.description: Measure and assess the progress made by the team.

activitySpaces.name: Stop The Work
activitySpaces.description: Shutdown the platform engineering endeavor and hand over the team's responsibilities.

activitySpaces.name: Establish Platform Governance
activitySpaces.description: Translating regulatory requirements into executable policy code.

activitySpaces.name: Organize Platform Engineering
activitySpaces.description: Structuring the platform teams and managing backlogs.

competencies.name: Stakeholder Representation
competencies.description: Ability to gather, communicate, and balance the needs of other stakeholders, and accurately represent their views.

competencies.name: Platform Strategic Alignment
competencies.description: Ability to synthesize business goals and organizational dynamics.

competencies.name: Analysis
competencies.description: Ability to understand opportunities and their related stakeholder needs, and transform them into an agreed and consistent set of requirements.

competencies.name: Engineering
competencies.description: Ability to design distributed systems and author Infrastructure as Code.

competencies.name: Leadership
competencies.description: Ability to inspire and motivate a group of people to achieve a successful conclusion to their work.

competencies.name: Management
competencies.description: Ability to coordinate, plan, and track the work done by a team.

competencies.name: Site Reliability
competencies.description: Ability to engineer observability telemetry and automate incident remediation.

competencies.name: Platform Security And Compliance Enforcement
competencies.description: The ability to design zero-trust perimeters, manage cryptographic keys, and author compliance-as-code.

practices.name: Team Topologies
practices.description: A practice based on the 'Team Topologies' framework by Matthew Skelton and Manuel Pais, focusing on optimizing team organization for fast flow and manageable cognitive load.

alphas.name: Team Cognitive Load
alphas.description: The total amount of mental effort being used in the working memory of a team.

states.name: Assessed
states.description: Current cognitive load for all teams is understood and documented.

checklist.name: Load Surveyed
checklist.description: Teams have been surveyed regarding their perceived cognitive load.

checklist.name: Bottlenecks Identified
checklist.description: Specific areas where cognitive load exceeds capacity are documented.

states.name: Bounded
states.description: Team responsibilities are restricted to match cognitive capacity.

checklist.name: Domain Split
checklist.description: Large domains have been split into smaller, manageable sub-domains.

checklist.name: Hand-offs Minimized
checklist.description: Inter-team hand-offs have been reduced to support autonomy.

states.name: Optimized
states.description: Teams focus primarily on their core mission with minimal extraneous friction.

checklist.name: Platform Support Active
checklist.description: Platform teams are successfully abstracting away low-level infrastructure complexity.

checklist.name: Flow Verified
checklist.description: Cycle time and lead time metrics show steady or improving flow.

alphas.name: Team Interaction Mode
alphas.description: The specific way two teams interact to achieve their goals.

states.name: Defined
states.description: The intended interaction modes between specific teams are selected.

checklist.name: Mode Selected
checklist.description: Either Collaboration, X-as-a-Service, or Facilitating is chosen for each team pair.

checklist.name: Duration Estimated
checklist.description: The expected duration of the chosen interaction mode is defined.

states.name: Active
states.description: Teams are interacting according to the defined mode.

checklist.name: Collaboration Sessions Held
checklist.description: If in collaboration mode, shared sessions are actively occurring.

checklist.name: Service Consumed
checklist.description: If X-as-a-Service, the consumer team is using the provider team's API/product.

states.name: Evolved
states.description: Interaction modes are adjusted based on organizational evolution.

checklist.name: Mode Transitioned
checklist.description: Teams have transitioned from Collaboration to X-as-a-Service as the product matured.

workProducts.name: Team API
workProducts.description: A description of how a team interacts with others, including communication channels, documentation, and technical interfaces.

levelsOfDetail.name: Drafted
levelsOfDetail.description: The basic components of the Team API are identified.

checklist.name: Communication Channels Listed
checklist.description: Slack channels, email lists, and office hours are documented.

checklist.name: Core Mission Stated
checklist.description: The team's primary purpose and scope are clearly written.

levelsOfDetail.name: Published
levelsOfDetail.description: The Team API is accessible to the entire organization and regularly updated.

checklist.name: Technical API Documented
checklist.description: For platform/enabling teams, technical service definitions are included.

checklist.name: Roadmap Shared
checklist.description: The team's future plans are visible to consumers.

workProducts.name: Team Type Map
workProducts.description: A visualization of the organization showing teams categorized by the four topologies.

levelsOfDetail.name: Initial Mapping
levelsOfDetail.description: Teams are roughly categorized into the four types.

checklist.name: Stream-Aligned Identified
checklist.description: Core value-stream teams are highlighted.

levelsOfDetail.name: Optimized Topology
levelsOfDetail.description: The organization design is aligned to minimize dependencies and hand-offs.

checklist.name: Platform Boundaries Defined
checklist.description: Clear boundaries between platform and stream-aligned teams are established.

activities.name: Classify Team Topologies
activities.description: Review existing team structures and re-align them into Stream-aligned, Enabling, Complicated Subsystem, or Platform teams.

activities.name: Define Team Interaction Agreements
activities.description: Establish formal agreements on how specific teams will work together (Collaboration, X-as-a-Service, or Facilitating).

activities.name: Implement Self-Service Platform APIs
activities.description: The platform team authors and exposes technical interfaces for stream-aligned teams to consume as a service.

workBreakdowns.name: Organizational Flow Assessment
workBreakdowns.description: The process of evaluating team cognitive load and interaction friction.

task.name: Survey Team Cognitive Load
task.description: Distribute and analyze cognitive load questionnaires to all engineering teams.

task.name: Map Existing Dependencies
task.description: Identify all cross-team blocking dependencies and hand-offs.

task.name: Formalize Team API Documentation
task.description: Creation of the Team API 'README' for a specific platform service.

complexity.name: Organizational Assessment Complexity
complexity.description: Measures the difficulty of changing team structures within a large enterprise.

practices.name: Site Reliability Engineering Practice
practices.description: This practice implements the principles of Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) as pioneered by Google and evolved by the industry. It focuses on balancing service reliability with the pace of innovation through Service Level Objectives (SLOs), Error Budgets, and the systematic elimination of toil.

alphas.name: Service Reliability
alphas.description: The degree to which a platform asset or service performs its intended function under specified conditions for a specified period.

states.name: Defined
states.description: Service Level Indicators (SLIs) and Objectives (SLOs) are documented for the service.

checklist.name: Critical user journeys identified
checklist.description: High-level tasks users perform are mapped.

checklist.name: Relevant SLIs selected
checklist.description: Latency, availability, errors, or saturation metrics chosen.

checklist.name: Target SLOs proposed
checklist.description: Target percentages established for each SLI.

checklist.name: Stakeholder sign-off achieved
checklist.description: Business and engineering agree on the reliability targets.

states.name: Instrumented
states.description: The service is capable of emitting the necessary telemetry to measure the defined SLIs.

checklist.name: Metrics collection active
checklist.description: Exporter or agent is sending telemetry to the monitoring system.

checklist.name: Data pipelines verified
checklist.description: The metrics reaching the database are accurate and timely.

checklist.name: SLO calculation logic codified
checklist.description: The formula for the SLO (good events / total events) is implemented in tools.

states.name: Observable
states.description: The current state of reliability is visible and actionable alerting is in place.

checklist.name: Real-time dashboards published
checklist.description: Current SLO status and Error Budget burn rate are visible.

checklist.name: Alerting thresholds configured
checklist.description: Alerts trigger based on significant budget burn, not just threshold spikes.

checklist.name: Notification channels established
checklist.description: On-call engineers receive alerts via integrated paging systems.

states.name: Managed
states.description: The Error Budget is used to make data-driven decisions about feature velocity vs. reliability work.

checklist.name: Error budget policy defined
checklist.description: Consequences for budget exhaustion (e.g., feature freeze) are agreed upon.

checklist.name: Budget burn reviewed weekly
checklist.description: Team analyzes why the budget was consumed and identifies trends.

checklist.name: Reliability backlog prioritized
checklist.description: Engineering effort is diverted to reliability when budget is thin.

states.name: Reliable
states.description: The service consistently meets or exceeds its SLOs and the team has sufficient capacity for innovation.

checklist.name: SLOs met over the rolling window
checklist.description: Success rate stays within targets for the last 28 days.

checklist.name: Toil is under 50% of workload
checklist.description: Operational manual work does not dominate engineering time.

checklist.name: Resiliency tested in production
checklist.description: Chaos experiments confirm the system's fault tolerance.

workProducts.name: SLO Specification
workProducts.description: A document defining the Service Level Indicators and their corresponding Objectives.

levelsOfDetail.name: Drafted
levelsOfDetail.description: Initial set of SLIs and proposed targets recorded.

checklist.name: User journeys mapped to SLIs
checklist.description: Visual or list-based mapping exists.

checklist.name: Thresholds specified
checklist.description: Numerical targets provided.

levelsOfDetail.name: Approved
levelsOfDetail.description: Formal agreement from product and engineering stakeholders.

checklist.name: Error budget consequences signed
checklist.description: Agreed-upon policy for budget exhaustion.

checklist.name: Review schedule established
checklist.description: Plan for iterating on the SLO as the service evolves.

workProducts.name: Blameless Postmortem
workProducts.description: A report detailing an incident, its causes, and actions to prevent recurrence without assigning blame to individuals.

levelsOfDetail.name: Contextualized
levelsOfDetail.description: Timeline and impact are clearly documented.

checklist.name: Sequence of events recorded
checklist.description: Minute-by-minute log of what happened.

checklist.name: Impact quantified
checklist.description: How many users were affected and for how long.

levelsOfDetail.name: Remediated
levelsOfDetail.description: Action items are created and tracked to closure.

checklist.name: Root causes (Five Whys) identified
checklist.description: The systemic failure points are found.

checklist.name: Preventative tasks scheduled
checklist.description: Tickets created in the engineering backlog.

activities.name: Define SLOs and SLIs
activities.description: The process of identifying what matters most to the users and quantifying it as a measurable target.

activities.name: Conduct Incident Response
activities.description: Managing the lifecycle of a production failure from detection to mitigation.

activities.name: Perform Blameless Postmortem Analysis
activities.description: Reviewing an incident to learn and improve system resilience.

activities.name: Eliminate Toil via Automation
activities.description: The systematic replacement of manual, repetitive tasks with automated software solutions.

workBreakdowns.name: SRE Foundation Setup
workBreakdowns.description: Core tasks to establish SRE practices on a new platform service.

complexity.name: SRE Complexity Profile
complexity.description: Evaluates the difficulty of instrumenting the target service.

task.name: Identify Critical User Journeys
task.description: Meet with Product Owners to determine the 3-5 most important things a user does.

task.name: Implement Telemetry Exporters
task.description: Modify service configuration or code to export metrics in a format like Prometheus.

task.name: Create SLO Dashboards
task.description: Build visualizations in Grafana or similar tool to track error budget burn.

task.name: Configure Multi-Window Multi-Burnrate Alerts
task.description: Set up sophisticated alerting to catch both fast and slow budget burns.

practices.name: Kubernetes Platform Fundamentals
practices.description: Architecting a Next-Generation Kubernetes Platform: A Comprehensive Practice Guide for Cloud-Native Engineering. The core objective of Platform Engineering is the conceptualization, creation, and continuous maintenance of an Internal Developer Platform (IDP).

alphas.name: Internal Developer Platform
alphas.description: An IDP operates as a curated, standardized, and self-service ecosystem that deliberately abstracts the underlying complexities of Kubernetes and the broader Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) technology landscape.

states.name: Provisional
states.description: The platform exists predominantly as a byproduct of immediate necessity.

checklist.name: Reactive Execution
checklist.description: Investment is voluntary or temporary, often handled by a tiger team reacting to acute infrastructure crises rather than executing a long-term vision.

checklist.name: Manual Interfaces
checklist.description: Adoption across the enterprise is erratic, and interfaces rely heavily on custom, manual processes—such as submitting IT helpdesk tickets.

states.name: Operational
states.description: Marks the introduction of dedicated funding and the establishment of permanent platform teams.

checklist.name: Established Cost Center
checklist.description: The organization treats the platform as an established cost center.

checklist.name: Extrinsic Push Adoption
checklist.description: Adoption at this stage is typically driven by an extrinsic push, meaning enterprise leadership mandates the use of the platform through compliance requirements or strict governance rules.

states.name: Scalable
states.description: The platform is no longer viewed as an IT support project, but as an internal software product.

checklist.name: Product Mindset
checklist.description: The platform team operates with a strict product management mindset, conducting user research and treating internal developers as their primary customers.

checklist.name: Intrinsic Pull
checklist.description: Adoption shifts from an extrinsic mandate to an intrinsic pull.

checklist.name: Self-Service
checklist.description: Interfaces transition to fully self-service portals, operations are centrally enabled with continuous delivery processes for platform features.

activities.name: Implement GitOps Automation
activities.description: GitOps treats a Git repository as the single, unassailable source of truth for all declarative infrastructure and application states, fundamentally eliminating the fragility of manual configuration and imperative script execution.

activities.name: Establish Golden Paths
activities.description: When developers choose to stay on the Golden Path, they bypass the need to configure complex underlying infrastructure, drastically accelerating their time-to-market.

workProducts.name: GitOps Repository Architecture
workProducts.description: Structuring the GitOps repositories to support multiple independent development teams safely sharing the same underlying Kubernetes clusters, a concept known as multi-tenancy.

checklist.name: Multi-Tenant Standard
checklist.description: The most resilient organizational pattern is the centralized, multi-tenant configuration.

checklist.name: Infrastructure Separation
checklist.description: Industry best practices mandate the strict separation of infrastructure code from application code.

checklist.name: Restricted Access
checklist.description: Application developers have absolutely no access to this repository.

checklist.name: Directory Hierarchies
checklist.description: Within a unified tenant repository, isolation is achieved via strict directory hierarchies.

workProducts.name: Golden Path Templates
workProducts.description: A pre-architected, fully supported approach to building, testing, and deploying a specific type of software.

checklist.name: Repository Generation
checklist.description: Automated scaffolding that instantly generates a foundational application codebase containing the organization's preferred directory structure.

checklist.name: Integrated Toolchains
checklist.description: Pre-configured CI/CD pipelines that automatically compile artifacts, execute unit and integration tests, and conduct static application security testing (SAST) without developer intervention.

checklist.name: Deployment Configured
checklist.description: Standardized Helm charts or Kustomize configurations that define exactly how the application runs within Kubernetes.

workBreakdowns.name: Kubernetes Platform Execution
workBreakdowns.description: Execution breakdown for deploying the core platform primitives and interfaces.

task.name: Design GitOps Tenant Repositories
task.description: A common standard is prefixing tenant directories with numerical identifiers (e.g., 01-payment-team, 02-auth-team).

task.name: Configure Golden Path Templates
task.description: Develop deployment manifests including default CPU and memory limits, readiness and liveness probes, and horizontal pod autoscaler parameters.

complexity.name: Platform Risk Profile
complexity.description: Assessing the systemic friction of standardizing across cloud-native domains.
